principal.definition: The amount borrowed that remains to be repaid, excluding interest.

interest.definition: The cost of borrowing, calculated using the balance and the applicable rate.

postponement.definition: Delaying principal payments for a set period. Interest may still be payable during that time.

instalment.definition: A scheduled payment under the financing arrangement.

maturity.definition: The date the remaining loan balance is scheduled to be fully repaid.

outstanding.definition: Principal still owing at the relevant date.

fixedRate.definition: A rate that does not change during the specified fixed-rate period.

cashFlow.definition: Money coming into and going out of the business.

amortisation.definition: Repayment of principal over a schedule.

capitalisedInterest.definition: Interest added to the amount owing. This does not occur in this demonstration.

definitions.principal: Your [[principal|principal]] is the amount borrowed that remains to be repaid, not counting [[interest|interest]]. A [[postponement|principal postponement]] delays principal payments for a set period; interest is still paid.
definitions.interest: [[interest|Interest]] is the cost of borrowing. Each month it is calculated on the [[outstanding|outstanding principal]] at the [[fixedRate|fixed rate]], so it stays higher while principal is not being repaid.
definitions.next-payment: An [[instalment|instalment]] is a scheduled payment. During the [[postponement|postponement]], each instalment covers [[interest|interest]] only; once principal payments resume, it covers [[principal|principal]] and interest.
definitions.maturity: The [[maturity|maturity date]] is when the remaining loan balance is scheduled to be fully repaid. Repaying [[principal|principal]] later moves this date later.
definitions.fees: This change has no fee in this example, but it does change the total [[interest|interest]] you pay, because the [[outstanding|outstanding principal]] is repaid more slowly.
definitions.rate: A [[fixedRate|fixed rate]] does not change during the fixed-rate period. Your monthly [[interest|interest]] still depends on the [[outstanding|outstanding principal]] it applies to.
definitions.debt: [[outstanding|Outstanding principal]] is the principal still owing at a given date. A [[postponement|principal postponement]] changes when you repay it, not how much [[principal|principal]] you repay.

principal.title: Lower payments, same debt
body: Postponing {count} principal payments of {monthly} moves {deferred} of principal later in the schedule. It is still owing.
Your payments from {from} to {to} are {relief} lower, not {deferred}, because interest stays at {interest} a month instead of decreasing.

interest.title: Why interest is higher
body: Under the original schedule, principal goes down by {monthly} each month, so interest falls a little every month.
Under the revised schedule, principal stays at {opening} until {resume}, so interest stays at {interest} a month. The difference from {from} to {to} is {extra3}.
Because the whole schedule shifts later, the extra interest continues until the end: {extra} in total, which already includes the {extra3}.

next-payment.title: What happens next
body: Your payments on {d2} and {d3} are also {interest}. On {resume}, principal payments resume and your payment becomes {first}.
These lower payments are temporary cash-flow relief. The postponed principal is still owing.

maturity.title: Why the final payment moves
body: Principal payments of {monthly} restart on {resume} instead of continuing from {firstDate}. Every later principal payment shifts by {period}.
The schedule therefore needs {n} more monthly payments and ends on {date}. Interest continues on the principal still owing during those months.

fees.title: No fee does not mean no cost
body: No fee is charged for this change in this fictional scenario.
The postponement still increases total interest over the remaining schedule by {extra}, and total remaining payments go from {originalTotal} to {revisedTotal}.

rate.title: Same rate, different interest
body: Your rate stays at {rate} under both schedules. This change does not reset, increase or reduce it.
Monthly interest differs only because the principal the rate applies to is different: it is not reduced during the postponement.

debt.title: Why a temporary payment reduction is not a reduction in debt
body: During the postponement, you pay interest only. Your principal stays at {opening} instead of going down by {monthly} each month.
After the {lastPostponed} payment, you still owe {deferred} more principal than under the original schedule: {revisedOwing} instead of {originalOwing}.
That principal is repaid later. Principal payments of {monthly} resume on {resume} and continue until {date}, {period} later than originally scheduled.
Because more principal is owing for longer, total interest over the remaining schedule is {extra} higher.
Nothing is cancelled or written off: the principal you repay over the remaining schedule is {principal} under both schedules.

answers.whatChanged: Your principal payments for {months} are postponed. During those months you pay interest only: {postInterest} a month. Principal payments resume on {resumeDate}, your final payment moves to {revMat}, and the postponed principal remains owing.
answers.purpose: This notice explains an approved change to your loan: you asked to postpone principal payments, and in this fictional scenario the change is approved and completed. It shows what changes, what stays the same and what to do next.
answers.purposeSeasonal: This notice explains an approved change to your loan. In this fictional scenario, you asked to postpone principal payments to manage a planned seasonal inventory build. It shows what changes, what stays the same and what to do next.
answers.effectiveDate: The change takes effect on {effective}. The first payment under the revised schedule is due on {nextDate}.
answers.nextPayment: Your next payment is {revNext} on {nextDate}. It covers interest only, because principal is postponed that month.
answers.lastPostponement: Your last payment in the postponement is {lastPost} on {lastPostDate}, interest only. Principal payments resume on {resumeDate}, when your payment is {firstResumed}.
answers.postponementPeriod: Your principal payments for {months} are postponed. You still pay {postInterest} of interest in each of those months, and principal payments of {monthlyPrincipal} restart on {resumeDate}.
answers.principalMeaning: Principal is the amount borrowed that remains to be repaid, not including interest. Here, {deferred} of principal is moved later in the schedule; it is still owed.
answers.continuingInterest: Interest continues during the postponement at the same {rate} fixed rate. Because no principal is repaid in those months, you pay {postInterest} of interest each month; only principal is postponed.
answers.whyRelief: {deferred} of principal is delayed. Because that principal isn’t reduced, you pay {extra3} more interest within those months than in the original schedule. So your payments are {reduction} lower, not {deferred}, and the {deferred} of principal remains owing.
answers.relief: From {from} to {to}, your payments total {revNear} instead of {origNear}: {reduction} lower. This is temporary cash-flow relief, not a reduction in what you owe. The postponed principal is still owed, and over the whole remaining term you pay {extraLife} more interest.
answers.totalCost: The revised schedule adds {extraLife} of interest over the remaining term. The {extra3} of extra interest from {from} to {to} is already included in that amount, so it isn’t added again. There is no change fee.
answers.maturity: Your final payment moves from {origMat} to {revMat}, because the postponed principal is repaid at the end of the schedule.
answers.totalPayments: Over the whole schedule, your payments total {revTotalFull} in the revised schedule, compared with {origTotalFull} in the original schedule. The difference is the {extraLife} of additional interest, which already includes the {extra3} of extra interest from {from} to {to}; the principal you repay is the same.
answers.paymentCount: The revised schedule has {revCount} monthly payments, from {nextDate} to {revMat}. The original schedule had {origCount}, ending on {origMat}. The extra payments repay the postponed principal.
answers.issueDate: This notice was issued on {issue}. The change takes effect on {effective}, and the first payment under the revised schedule is due on {nextDate}.
answers.loanAmount: Both illustrated schedules start from {principalStartFull} of principal on {effective}. This sample notice covers that principal only; it doesn’t show your original loan amount or a live account balance.
answers.yearPayments: Your payments for {year} are listed month by month in “{payments}”, which groups the schedule by year and shows the original and revised totals for each year.
answers.resume: Principal payments resume on {resumeDate}. That payment is {firstResumed}: {monthlyPrincipal} of principal plus {firstResumedInterest} of interest.
answers.rate: Your fixed rate stays at {rate}; it doesn’t change. Total interest rises only because principal is repaid later.
answers.fees: There is no fee for this change in this fictional scenario. The cost of the postponement is the additional interest of {extraLife} over the remaining term.
answers.unchanged: Your {rate} fixed rate, the {monthlyPrincipal} monthly principal instalment once payments resume, and all other terms of loan {loanId} stay the same. There is no change fee.
answers.acceptance: You don’t need to accept, sign or reply to anything through this notice; the change is already approved and completed in this fictional scenario. It’s a good idea to review the revised schedule and update your cash-flow planning.
answers.printExport: In “{notice}”, choose “{print}” for a printable copy, or download the original or revised schedule as a CSV file. In “{payments}”, you can also download the selection you’re viewing.
answers.queryPrep: Choose “{askItem}” beside any item, or “{askGeneral}” in “{help}”. You draft your question, review it, then create a local demo request. Nothing is sent to BDC in this demo.
answers.support: The “{supportSection}” section lists optional BDC resources, such as financial management consulting for cash-flow planning. They’re separate from this notice and don’t imply eligibility or approval.
answers.supportSuppressed: The “{supportSection}” section focuses on help and learning resources, such as cash-flow planning. They’re separate from this notice and don’t imply eligibility or approval.
answers.debtReduced: The postponement delays {deferred} of principal; it doesn’t reduce or cancel your debt. You still owe the same principal, and it’s repaid later in the schedule.
answers.capitalisedInterest: No interest is capitalised. Interest during the postponement is paid each month, so it isn’t added to the amount you owe.
answers.balanceAfter: At the end of the postponement ({postEnd}), the revised schedule shows {revPostClose} of principal still owing, compared with {origPostClose} in the original schedule. This demo doesn’t show a live account balance.
answers.accountant: You can share a printed copy or the CSV schedule with your accountant. In a live service, an authorised user could be given controlled access; this demo can’t grant access to anyone.
answers.aboutClair: I’m Clair, a demo assistant. I answer from this sample notice using local rules: there’s no live AI connection, and what you type stays in this browser. I can’t see any real BDC records.
answers.aboutDemo: Demo insights show local interaction counts from this browser tab only. They aren’t measured BDC outcomes, and nothing is sent anywhere.
answers.greeting: Hello! Ask me anything about this sample notice, such as what changed or when your next payment is.
answers.thanks: You’re welcome. Is there anything else in this notice I can explain?
answers.scheduleClause: This schedule lists all {revCount} revised payments, from {nextDate} to {revMat}. The first payments are interest only; the rest include {monthlyPrincipal} of principal each month.
answers.assumptions: The illustration assumes month-end payments, a fixed {rate} rate, no new advances or extra repayments, and no capitalised interest. These are simulation assumptions, not BDC servicing rules.
answers.chartPayments: The chart compares monthly payments from {from} to {sixth}. In the revised schedule, the {from} to {to} payments are interest only ({postInterest}); from {resumeMonth}, payments include {monthlyPrincipal} of principal again.
answers.chartBalance: In the revised schedule, principal stays at {principalStart} until the end of {postEnd}, then falls by {monthlyPrincipal} a month until {revMat}. In the original schedule, it reaches zero on {origMat}.
answers.resourceFinancialManagement: Financial management consulting can help with cash-flow forecasting and working-capital planning. It’s optional support, separate from this notice, and doesn’t imply eligibility.
answers.resourceFinancialManagementSeasonal: Financial management consulting can help with cash-flow forecasting and working-capital planning, which matters for a planned seasonal inventory build. It’s optional support, separate from this notice, and doesn’t imply eligibility.
answers.resourceWorkingCapital: A Working Capital Loan is a separate BDC financing product, listed in “{supportSection}” for information only. It isn’t part of this notice, any financing is subject to assessment and approval, and I can’t assess eligibility.
answers.resourceWorkingCapitalSuppressed: Additional borrowing isn’t promoted in this situation. If you’re facing difficulties, you can prepare a question for a person to discuss help.
answers.resourceLearning: BDC’s cash-flow learning resources are educational. They can help you plan around lower payments from {from} to {to}, without any credit commitment.
answers.limitChange: I can’t change your payments or loan terms; I can only explain this sample notice. If you’d like to discuss a change, you can prepare a question for a person.
answers.limitApprove: I can’t approve another postponement or any other request. You can prepare a question for a person instead; in this demo, nothing is sent to BDC.
answers.limitEligibility: I can’t assess eligibility or offer financing. The “{supportSection}” section describes optional BDC resources, and any financing is subject to assessment and approval. You can also prepare a question for a person.
answers.limitEligibilitySuppressed: I can’t assess eligibility or offer financing. If you’re facing difficulties, you can prepare a question for a person to discuss help that fits your situation.
answers.limitPay: I can’t process payments, and this demo has no payment function. Under the revised schedule, your next payment is {revNext} on {nextDate}.
answers.hardship: I can’t change your payments or tell you what happens if a payment is missed; this sample notice doesn’t cover that. If you’re having trouble making a payment, it’s best to talk to someone about your situation: you can prepare a question for a person.

a: You asked for a temporary [[postponement|principal postponement]] to help manage a planned seasonal inventory build. In this fictional scenario, the change is approved and complete. This notice explains how your repayment schedule changes as a result, starting {effectiveDate}.
It shows what changes, what stays the same and what, if anything, you need to do. It is not a new offer, and you do not need to sign anything.
No. In this scenario, the change is already approved and complete, and no acceptance is required through this notice.
We suggest you review the revised schedule and update your [[cashFlow|cash-flow]] planning, especially for the return to a {first} payment on {resume}.
“Mark as reviewed” on the overview is an optional local note in this demo. It is not acceptance, consent or proof of understanding.
No. The {deferred} of principal you would have repaid from {from} to {to} is postponed. It remains owing and is repaid later in the schedule.
After your {from} to {to} payments, your [[outstanding|outstanding principal]] is still {balanceAfter}. The revised schedule has {revCount} payments instead of {origCount} and ends on {revMaturity}.
Over the remaining schedule, total [[interest|interest]] increases by {extra}. Lower payments from {from} to {to} are temporary [[cashFlow|cash-flow]] relief, not a reduction in what you owe.
No. The demonstration [[fixedRate|fixed rate]] stays at {rate} a year. Only the timing of principal payments changes.
Total interest increases only because principal is repaid later, so the balance stays higher for longer. The rate itself does not change.

capitalised.q: Is unpaid interest added to my balance?
a: No. Interest is paid every month during the postponement, so nothing is added to what you owe. There is no [[capitalisedInterest|capitalised interest]] in this scenario.
Your [[outstanding|outstanding principal]] stays at {principal} from {from} to {to}, then goes down by {monthly} with each payment from {resume}.
Your next payment is {next}, due on {nextDate}. It is interest only, because no [[principal|principal]] is due from {from} to {to}.
Under the original schedule, that payment would have been {nextOriginal}. The same {interest} interest-only payment applies at the end of each month from {fromY} to {toY}.
Payments are not processed in this demonstration.
Yes. Only [[principal|principal]] payments are postponed. [[interest|Interest]] is still charged and paid every month: {interest} with each payment from {fromY} to {toY}.
Because the [[outstanding|outstanding principal]] stays at {principal} during those months, the interest does not go down the way it would have under the original schedule.

relief.q: Why is the relief {relief} rather than {deferred}?
a: You postpone {deferred} of [[principal|principal]] payments from {from} to {to} ({period} at {monthly}). Because the principal does not go down during those months, [[interest|interest]] stays at {interest} a month instead of gradually decreasing. That adds {extra3} of interest over those {period}.
So your payments over that period total {revNear} instead of {origNear}: {deferred} minus {extra3} equals {relief} lower.
The {extra3} is already part of the {extra} increase in total interest over the remaining schedule. It is not an extra cost on top of it.
Principal payments restart on {resume}. That payment is {first}: {monthly} of [[principal|principal]] plus {firstInterest} of [[interest|interest]].
After that, you repay {monthly} of principal each month, plus interest on the [[outstanding|outstanding principal]], until the final payment on {revMaturity}.

final-payment.q: When is my final payment now?
a: Your final payment moves from {origMaturity} to {revMaturity}, {period} later. The [[maturity|maturity date]] changes because the postponed principal is repaid at the end of the schedule.
The revised schedule has {revCount} monthly payments instead of {origCount}. The last one is {finalPayment}.
No change fee applies in this scenario: the fee is {fee}.
The cost of the postponement is the additional interest: {extra} over the remaining schedule, already included in the revised schedule.

ask.q: How do I ask a question?
a: Use “{askLabel}” on this page, or “{askAbout}” beside a card, payment or notice paragraph. The form keeps the item you selected, so you don’t have to explain the context again.
In this demonstration, the form creates a local demo request only. Nothing is sent to BDC.
For a quick explanation, you can also ask Clair, the demo assistant. Clair answers from this sample notice only, using local rules, with no live AI connection.
Yes, you can share what you see here. For example, print the notice or export the revised schedule as a CSV file so your accountant can check it against your records.
This demonstration cannot give anyone access to an account. There is no sign-in, no user management and no connection to BDC systems.
BDC’s published Client Space describes controlled shared access for people you authorise. In a production version, the intended journey would be:
- You would authorise your accountant through BDC’s own secure process for shared access.
- Your accountant would sign in with their own credentials, never yours.
- They would see the notice and schedules you chose to share, and could prepare questions about them.
Never share your own sign-in details, even with your accountant.

print-export.q: Can I print or export the schedule?
a: Yes. In “{noticeTab}”, use “{printLabel}” for a print layout with the notice, its record details and the revised schedule.
In “{paymentsTab}”, you can download the displayed months or the full revised schedule as a CSV file.
A browser-generated PDF is a convenience copy of this demonstration, not a certified record.

purpose.p1: This notice confirms an amendment to the repayment terms of loan {loan} for {company} and describes its effect on your payments, interest and final payment date. It is the formal reference for the plain-language explanations in this demonstration.
purpose.p2: This is a synthetic notice prepared for a concept demonstration. The client, the loan and all amounts are fictional. It is not an actual BDC notice, offer or agreement.

amendment.p1Seasonal: At the request of the client, {company}, and to support a planned seasonal inventory build, a temporary [[postponement|principal postponement]] on loan {loan} has been approved and completed in this fictional scenario. The amendment takes effect on {effective}.
amendment.p1: At the request of the client, {company}, a temporary [[postponement|principal postponement]] on loan {loan} has been approved and completed in this fictional scenario. The amendment takes effect on {effective}.
amendment.p2: The amendment changes when principal is repaid. It does not change the interest rate or reduce the principal owing.
amendment.acceptance: Customer acceptance required through this notice

postponement.p1: The [[principal|principal]] payments otherwise due in {months} are postponed. For each of these months, the principal payable is {zero}.
postponement.p2: In total, {deferred} of principal is postponed. This principal is not cancelled or reduced: it remains owing and is repaid in later instalments under the revised schedule.

interest.p1: [[interest|Interest]] continues to accrue on the outstanding principal of {opening} at the [[fixedRate|fixed annual rate]] of {rate}, and is payable monthly during the postponement period.
interest.p2: Each payment due during the postponement period is {interest}, consisting entirely of interest. Because no principal is repaid during this period, the monthly interest does not decrease.
interest.p3: No interest is [[capitalisedInterest|capitalised]] (added to the principal) as a result of this amendment.

resumption.p1: Principal payments resume with the payment due on {resume}. From that date, each monthly payment consists of a principal [[instalment|instalment]] of {monthly} plus interest on the outstanding principal.
resumption.p2: The first resumed payment, due on {resume}, is {first}: {monthly} of principal and {firstInterest} of interest. The interest portion then decreases each month as principal is repaid.

maturity.p1: The final payment date ([[maturity|maturity date]]) changes from {original} to {revised}.
maturity.p2: The revised schedule has {revCount} monthly payments starting {firstDate}, instead of {origCount} under the original schedule.

cost.p1: Because principal is repaid later, more interest is payable over the remaining schedule. Compared with the original schedule:
cost.totalInterest: Total interest over the complete remaining schedule increases from {origInt} to {revInt}, an increase of {extra}.
cost.totalPayments: Total remaining payments increase from {origTotal} to {revTotal}.
cost.nearTerm: Payments due from {from} to {to} total {revNear} instead of {origNear}, a reduction of {relief}. This equals the {deferred} of postponed principal less {extra3} of additional interest payable during those months.
cost.partOf: The {extra3} of additional interest payable during those months forms part of the {extra} increase in total interest. It is not charged in addition to it.
cost.sameAmount: In this example, the payments due from {from} to {to} ({revNear}) and the increase in total interest ({extra}) happen to be the same amount. They measure different things.
cost.p2: The postponed principal of {deferred} remains owing. This amendment does not cancel or reduce any amount owing.

unchanged.p1: This amendment changes only the timing of principal repayment described above. The following remain unchanged:
unchanged.rate: The fixed annual interest rate of {rate}.
unchanged.instalment: The monthly principal instalment of {monthly}, once principal payments resume.
unchanged.fee: No fee is charged for this amendment (change fee: {fee}).
unchanged.other: All other terms and conditions of loan {loan}.

action.p1: Please review this notice and the revised repayment schedule, and update your internal cash-flow planning to reflect the new payment amounts and dates.
action.p2: No acceptance, signature or reply is required through this notice. This document does not process any payment, and no payment can be made through it.
action.p3: Your next payment under the revised schedule is {next} on {nextDate}.

schedule.p1: The revised schedule below lists all {count} remaining monthly payments, from {firstDate} to {lastDate}. It replaces the original schedule from the effective date, {effective}.

assumptions.p1: The schedules in this notice are an illustration based on the following simulation assumptions. They are not actual BDC servicing conventions.

contact.p1: For questions about this notice, use Help & questions in this demonstration to read answers to common questions, look up terms in the glossary or prepare a question about a specific clause. You can also ask Clair, the demo assistant, to explain any clause.
